heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Bhutan
heroData.subtitle: Hire in Bhutan without a local entity
heroData.description: Navigate Bhutan's unique layout laws and employment regulations using an Employer of Record. Launch in Thimphu in as little as 2 weeks.

steps.title: Requirement Assessment
steps.description: Define the role, salary in Ngultrum (BTN), and benefits. EOR partner reviews compliance with the Labour and Employment Act of Bhutan 2007.

steps.title: Employee Agreement
steps.description: Drafting of a compliant employment contract. Mandatory inclusion of provident fund (PF) details and defined working hours (8 hours/day).

steps.title: KYC and Registration
steps.description: Collection of employee documents (CID, Tax Payer Number). Registration with the National Pension and Provident Fund (NPPF).

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Employee is legally hired by the EOR. Payroll setup is finalized with the Department of Revenue and Customs (DRC).

items.title: Permanent Establishment Risk
items.text: Using an EOR for long-term commercial activities (18+ months) may trigger Permanent Establishment (PE) risks, requiring a local entity.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Standard probation period in Bhutan is 6 months. Termination during this period requires 7 days notice.

items.title: Currency Peg
items.text: The Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN) is pegged 1:1 to the Indian Rupee (INR), providing stability for regional transactions.

items.title: Working Hours
items.text: Standard corporate hours are 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday through Friday. Government offices are closed on weekends.

items.title: Dress Code
items.text: Formal wear (Gho/Kira) is mandatory in government offices, but Western business attire is standard in the private tech sector.

items.title: Holidays
items.text: Expect closures during major festivals (Tshechus). Plan imperative meetings around the lunar calendar.

faqs.question: Can EOR employees in Bhutan work remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, remote work is legally permitted. However, the EOR must ensure the workspace meets basic safety standards outlined in the Labour Act.

faqs.question: What are the mandatory benefits?
faqs.answer: Mandatory benefits include Provident Fund (PF) contributions (min 5-10% employer match) and Gratuity payments after 10 years of service.

faqs.question: Is health insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: While Bhutan has free public healthcare, supplemental private health insurance is a common competitive benefit for tech and professional roles.

steps.title: Attendance & Leave Data
steps.description: Collate working days, paid leave, and overtime (calculated at 1.5x for normal overtime, 2x for night/holidays).

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Apply Personal Income Tax (PIT) slabs. Deduct Provident Fund (PF) and Insurance (GIS) contributions.

steps.title: Disbursement
steps.description: Net salary transferred to employee bank accounts (Bank of Bhutan, BNBL) by the 30th of the month.

steps.title: Filing
steps.description: Remit TDS to DRC and PF contributions to NPPF by the 15th of the following month.

rows.label: Gratuity Fund
values: 1 month salary per year (payable after 10 yrs)

items.title: 13th Month Pay
items.text: There is no statutory requirement for 13th-month pay in Bhutan, but performance bonuses are common in the private sector.

items.title: TDS Penalties
items.text: Late deposit of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) attracts a penalty of 24% p.a. interest plus fines.

items.title: Minimum Wage
items.text: The national minimum daily wage rate is Nu 375, though professional sectors demand significantly higher rates.

items.title: Local Banks
items.text: Bank of Bhutan (BoB) and Bhutan National Bank (BNB) are the primary institutions for salary accounts.

items.title: Digital Transfers
items.text: mBoB and other mobile banking apps are widely used for instant transfers and salary usage.

items.title: Forex
items.text: Paying salaries directly in USD to local accounts requires specific RMA (Royal Monetary Authority) approval.

faqs.question: What is the tax year in Bhutan?
faqs.answer: The income year generally follows the calendar year (Jan-Dec) for Personal Income Tax.

faqs.question: How is overtime calculated?
faqs.answer: Overtime is paid at 50% premium for weekdays and 100% premium for rest days and public holidays.

faqs.question: Are payslips mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, employers must provide a written payslip (digital is accepted) detailing gross pay, deductions, and net pay.

values: On excess over 1M (+ 10% surcharge on tax if >1M)

items.title: Deductions
items.text: Education allowance (up to Nu 350,000 per child) and Life Insurance premiums are deductible before tax calculation.

items.title: Surcharge
items.text: A 10% surcharge on the tax amount applies if net taxable income exceeds Nu 1,000,000.

items.title: Provident Fund
items.text: Employee contribution (min 5%, usually 10%) is deducted from Gross Salary before Tax calculation.

steps.title: Determine Gross Salary
steps.description: Start with annual gross salary (e.g., Nu 600,000).

steps.title: Less Deductions
steps.description: Deduct PF (e.g., 10% = 60k). Net Taxable Income = 540k.

steps.title: Calculate Net
steps.description: Net Pay = Gross - PF - Tax = 600k - 60k - 31k = 509,000.

items.title: Regional Comparison
items.text: Bhutan's tax rates are generally lower than India's, making it attractive for high-income earners.

items.title: Online Tools
items.text: The DRC provides an official online tax calculator on their website for precise assessments.

items.title: Changes
items.text: Tax rates were revised in 2021. Ensure you are using the latest slabs (2024-25).

faqs.question: Does this include bonuses?
faqs.answer: Yes, bonuses usually form part of taxable income in the year received.

faqs.question: Is the currency pegged?
faqs.answer: Yes, 1 Nu = 1 INR. Indian Rupee is widely accepted in Bhutan.

faqs.question: How often is tax deducted?
faqs.answer: Employers must deduct TDS monthly based on the estimated annual liability.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Bhutan
heroData.subtitle: FDI and Local Company Setup
heroData.description: Register your Private Limited Company or FDI project in Bhutan. Navigate Ministry of Economic Affairs clearances.

steps.title: FDI Registration
steps.description: For foreign investors: Submit Foreign Direct Investment Registration Application (FDIRA) to the Department of Industry.

steps.title: Name Clearance
steps.description: Apply for name availability with the Company Registry, Ministry of Economic Affairs.

steps.title: Incorporation Documents
steps.description: Draft Articles of Incorporation. Submit to the Registrar along with Security Clearance of Directors.

steps.title: Business License
steps.description: Obtain specific operating license from the Regional Trade and Industry Office.

items.title: FDI Floor
items.text: Service sector FDI typically requires a minimum project cost of Nu 5 Million (approx $60k USD).

items.title: Restricted Sectors
items.text: Media, distribution, and small-scale retail are generally restricted. IT and High-end Tourism are priority sectors.

items.title: Ownership
items.text: 100% foreign equity is permitted in IT/ITES and high-end education services. Other sectors may require a local partner (max 74% foreign equity).

items.title: Director Residency
items.text: Private Limited companies do not strictly require a resident director, but having a local contact facilitates banking.

items.title: Address
items.text: A registered office address in Bhutan is mandatory. Virtual offices are not yet widely recognized.

items.title: Renewals
items.text: Business licenses must be renewed annually by June 30th to avoid late fees.

faqs.question: What is the minimum capital for a Private Limited Company?
faqs.answer: Standard minimum paid-up capital is typically Nu 1,000,000 for FDI companies, subject to sector specifics.

faqs.question: Can I open a bank account before incorporation?
faqs.answer: You can open a temporary capital deposit account to deposit the equity, but a full operational account requires the Certificate of Incorporation.

faqs.question: How long does the process take?
faqs.answer: FDI approval plus incorporation typically takes 4-8 weeks, depending on sector clearances.

heroData.title: Staffing & Recruitment
heroData.subtitle: Hiring Top Talent in Bhutan
heroData.description: Access Bhutan's emerging English-speaking workforce, skilled in IT, tourism, and administration.

steps.title: Job Posting
steps.description: Advertise on Kuensel Online, Bhutan Jobs, or LinkedIn. Local newspapers are still highly effective.

steps.title: Screening
steps.description: Review CVs. Bhutanese education certificates (RUB) are standard. English proficiency is generally high.

steps.title: Interviews
steps.description: Conduct virtual or in-person interviews. Technical assessments are recommended for IT roles.

steps.title: Offer & NOC
steps.description: Extend offer. For expats, a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the MoLHR is required.

items.title: Youth Literacy
items.text: Youth literacy rate is over 93%, with a strong focus on digital skills in recent government programs.

items.title: Thimphu TechPark
items.text: The primary hub for IT talent. Companies located here get access to a concentrated pool of developers.

items.title: Brain Drain
items.text: Significant emigration of skilled youth to Australia/Canada is a current labor market challenge.

items.title: Language
items.text: English is the medium of instruction in schools, making it the primary business language.

items.title: References
items.text: Reference checks are common and effective due to the close-knit nature of society.

items.title: Inclusion
items.text: Bhutanese workplaces value harmony and respect. Aggressive negotiation styles may be counterproductive.

faqs.question: Are background checks legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, Security Clearance Certificates (SCC) from the Royal Bhutan Police are standard for employment.

faqs.question: What is the standard notice period?
faqs.answer: One month notice is standard for both employer and employee after the probation period.

faqs.question: Can I hire expats?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must prove that the skill is not available locally. Work permits are issued by the Department of Immigration.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions
heroData.subtitle: Digitizing HR in Bhutan
heroData.description: Implement modern HR tech stacks for attendance, payroll, and performance management compliant with Bhutanese rules.

steps.title: Needs Analysis
steps.description: Identify if you need simple attendance tracking (fingerprint/app) or full payroll integration.

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Choose between global platforms (Deel, Rippling) or regional/Indian solutions (Zoho, Keka) which are popular.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Import employee data. Ensure fields for CID, TPN, and PF numbers are custom-mapped.

steps.title: Training
steps.description: Train HR staff and employees on self-service portals.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: 4G/5G coverage is widespread in urban areas, supporting mobile-first HR apps.

items.title: Integration
items.text: Look for systems that can export tax reports in formats compatible with the RAMIS (Revenue Administration Management Information System).

items.title: Data Privacy
items.text: Ensure the vendor complies with emerging digital data security norms in Bhutan.

items.title: Mobile First
items.text: Most employees access internet via mobile. Ensure the HRIS has a robust Android/iOS app.

items.title: Digital SignatusES
items.text: Digital signatures are gaining legal weight, facilitating paperless HR processes.

items.title: Training
items.text: Invest time in training staff, as formal HRIS usage may be new to some employees.

faqs.question: Is biometric attendance legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, widely used in Bhutan. Consent should be obtained.

faqs.question: Can HRIS handle Bhutanese holidays?
faqs.answer: Most systems allow custom holiday calendars. Bhutan has regional holidays (e.g., Thimphu Drubchen) that need manual configuration.

faqs.question: Do I need a local server?
faqs.answer: No, cloud-based SaaS solutions are the standard and fully accepted.

heroData.title: Accounting Services
heroData.subtitle: BAS Compliant Bookkeeping
heroData.description: Maintain books according to Bhutanese Accounting Standards (BAS). Audit and financial reporting services.

steps.title: Bookkeeping
steps.description: Daily recording of transactions. Tally Prime is the dominant software used.

steps.title: BAS Compliance
steps.description: Ensure classification aligns with Bhutanese Accounting Standards 2020 (based on IFRS).

steps.title: Annual Closing
steps.description: Close books by Dec 31st. Prepare financial statements for audit.

steps.title: Filing
steps.description: Submit audited accounts to the Registrar of Companies and Tax Returns to DRC by March 31st.

items.title: BAS 2020
items.text: Bhutan has moved to BAS 2020, which is closely aligned with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

items.title: Audit Requirement
items.text: All registered companies (Private Ltd, Public Ltd) must undergo an annual statutory audit by a certified auditor.

items.title: Fiscal Year
items.text: The Income Year matches the calendar year (Jan 1 - Dec 31). Tax filing deadline is March 31st.

items.title: Currency
items.text: Accounting records must be maintained in Ngultrum. Exceptions exist for FDI companies for reporting purposes.

items.title: Documentation
items.text: Maintain physical copies of invoices/receipts for at least 5 years for tax audit purposes.

items.title: Bank Reconciliation
items.text: Reconcile frequently. Cross-border payments can have value dates differing from transaction dates.

faqs.question: Can I keep records in USD?
faqs.answer: Books must generally be maintained in Ngultrum (BTN). For FDI, dual currency reporting may be needed for parent consolidation.

faqs.question: What software is best?
faqs.answer: Tally is the industry standard. QuickBooks and Xero are gaining traction among startups and FDIs.

faqs.question: Who can audit my company?
faqs.answer: Only auditors registered with the Accounting and Auditing Standards Board of Bhutan (AASBB) can sign reports.

steps.title: AGM
steps.description: Hold Annual General Meeting within 6 months of financial year-end.

steps.title: Annual Return
steps.description: File Annual Return with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

steps.title: License Renewal
steps.description: Renew Business License annually with the MoEA (usually by June 30th).

steps.title: Environmental Clearance
steps.description: Renew Environmental Clearance (EC) if applicable to the industry.

items.title: Fronting
items.text: "Fronting" (leasing a license to another party) is strictly prohibited and carries heavy penalties and license cancellation.

items.title: Labour Inspections
items.text: MoLHR conducts periodic inspections for workplace safety, payroll records, and foreign worker permits.

items.title: Digital Signatures
items.text: Digital signatures are increasingly accepted for e-filing returns and applications.

items.title: Transparency
items.text: Bhutan ranks well for transparency. Government processes are rule-bound and relatively corruption-free.

items.title: Online Services
items.text: Most compliance filings (G2B services) can be done online through the G2C portal.

items.title: Sector Clearances
items.text: Specific sectors (education, tourism, health) need valid clearances from respective councils to renew business licenses.

faqs.question: Do I need a local director?
faqs.answer: The Companies Act does not strictly ban foreign directors, but at least one director typically handles local compliance. FDIs often appoint a local representative.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for non-compliance?
faqs.answer: Penalties range from daily fines for late filing to de-registration of the company for persistent non-compliance.

faqs.question: Are there industry specific compliances?
faqs.answer: Yes, Tourism companies need TCB (Tourism Council) certification. Construction firms need CDB registration.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Obtain Tax Payer Number (TPN) from Department of Revenue and Customs (DRC).

steps.title: TDS Deduction
steps.description: Deduct tax at source for salaries, contract payments (2-3%), and rents. Deposit monthly.

steps.title: Provisional Tax
steps.description: Large entities may need to pay advance tax instalments if applicable.

steps.title: Annual Filing
steps.description: File CIT and PIT returns online via RAMIS by March 31st.

items.title: Tax Holidays
items.text: Specific tax holidays exist for newly established CSIs (Cottage and Small Industries) and IT Park businesses.

items.title: Green Tax
items.text: Green tax applies to fuel and vehicle imports. Keeping operations eco-friendly can reduce indirect tax burden.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Related party transactions are scrutinized. Maintain documentation to prove arms-length pricing.

items.title: Business Expenses
items.text: All legitimate business expenses incurred to earn income are deductible.

items.title: Start-up Costs
items.text: Pre-operation costs can often be amortized over the first few years of operation.

items.title: Donations
items.text: Donations are only deductible if made to approved Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) up to 5% of taxable income.

faqs.question: Is there VAT in Bhutan?
faqs.answer: Bhutan currently uses a Sales Tax system on specific goods/services, moving towards a GST model (implementation deferred).

faqs.question: What is the CIT rate for FDIs?
faqs.answer: Standard CIT is 30%. However, fiscal incentives may reduce this for the first few years of operation in priority sectors.

faqs.question: Does Bhutan have double tax treaties?
faqs.answer: Bhutan has a Tax Treaty with India. Treaties with other nations are limited, so withholding taxes apply.

heroData.title: Legal & Advisory
heroData.subtitle: MSA, FDI, and Commercial Law
heroData.description: Expert legal drafting for Master Service Agreements, JV agreements, and FDI project proposals.

steps.title: Drafting
steps.description: Draft agreements under Bhutanese Law (Contract Act of Bhutan 2013). English is the standard language for business contracts.

steps.title: Review
steps.description: Review for compliance with FDI Policy and Consumer Protection Act.

steps.title: Stamping
steps.description: Affix legal stamps. Contracts are generally admissible in court if properly stamped and witnessed.

steps.title: Notarization
steps.description: Notarization by a Drangpon (Judge) or Notary Public for international validity.

items.title: Dispute Resolution
items.text: The Bhutan Alternative Dispute Resolution Centre (BADRC) handles arbitration. Courts are the second recourse.

items.title: Foreign Land Ownership
items.text: Foreigners strictly cannot own land. Long-term leases (up to 30 years) are the mechanism for FDI projects.

items.title: Governing Law
items.text: For local operations, Bhutanese law must govern. For cross-border MSAs, arbitration in neutral venues (Singapore) can sometimes be negotiated.

items.title: Stamp Duty
items.text: Legal stamps must be affixed to make an agreement legally binding in court.

items.title: Notary
items.text: Documents for use outside Bhutan (e.g., Parent company board resolutions) must be notarized.

items.title: Language
items.text: While English is standard, ensure court submissions are accompanied by Dzongkha translations if required.

faqs.question: Are electronic contracts valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the Information, Communications and Media Act, electronic contracts are generally recognized.

faqs.question: Can I sue in Bhutanese courts?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the process can be slow. Arbitration is preferred for commercial disputes.

faqs.question: Is IP protected?
faqs.answer: Bhutan has an Industrial Property Act. Trademarks and copyrights should be registered with the Department of Intellectual Property.

heroData.title: Software Development
heroData.subtitle: Outsourcing & Tech Solutions
heroData.description: Collaborate with Bhutan's growing tech sector. Custom development, app building, and IT services at Thimphu TechPark.

steps.title: RFP & Vendor Search
steps.description: Release RFP. Major vendors are located in Thimphu TechPark.

steps.title: Pilot Project
steps.description: Start with a small scope. Agile methodology is becoming common.

steps.title: Development
steps.description: Development phase. English communication is excellent among developers.

steps.title: Deployment
steps.description: Cloud deployment (AWS/Azure) or local hosting in Bhutan Telecom data centers.

items.title: Thimphu TechPark
items.text: The country's flagship IT park offering reliable power, internet, and office space for IT firms.

items.title: Skills
items.text: Strong capabilities in Web Dev (React, Node), Python, and specific focus on Blockchain (Druk Holding and Investments initiatives).

items.title: Scale
items.text: The talent pool is small. large scale projects (100+ devs) may be hard to staff locally.

items.title: Electricity
items.text: Power is cheap and reliable (green hydroelectricity), with very low downtime.

items.title: Internet
items.text: Fiber connectivity is good in Thimphu. Latency to SE Asia is reasonable.

items.title: Hardware
items.text: Specialized hardware may need to be imported from India or Thailand, which can take time.

faqs.question: How is the internet reliability?
faqs.answer: Reliable in Thimphu and TechPark with redundant fiber links globally. Rural areas may vary.

faqs.question: What is the time zone?
faqs.answer: Bhutan Time (BTT) is GMT+6. It overlaps well with Asia and Europe working hours.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives for software exports?
faqs.answer: Yes, IT companies in the TechPark often enjoy tax holidays and exemption from customs duties on hardware imports.

heroData.title: Marketing Agencies
heroData.subtitle: Digital & Creative Services
heroData.description: Reach the Bhutanese audience. Social media management, video production, and influencer marketing in Thimphu.

steps.title: Strategy
steps.description: Define audience. Urban youth are highly digital.

steps.title: Channel Selection
steps.description: Facebook is the dominant platform. Instagram and TikTok are growing rapidly.

steps.title: Content Creation
steps.description: Localize content. Dzongkha is the national language, but English is widely used in advertising.

steps.title: Execution
steps.description: Launch ads. Influencer collaborations (Bhutanese bloggers/vloggers) are high-impact.

items.title: Facebook Dominance
items.text: Facebook is the internet for many Bhutanese, used for news, business, and social connection (>85% share).

items.title: Influencers
items.text: Micro-influencers in fashion, travel, and food have high engagement and trust.

items.title: Cultural Sensitivity
items.text: Respect Buddhist traditions. Avoid using religious iconography inappropriately in commercial ads.

items.title: Demographics
items.text: The population is young, with a strong interest in global trends, technology, and Korean culture (K-Pop/K-Drama influence).

items.title: Trust
items.text: Word of mouth is powerful. Positive reviews on community Facebook groups drive significant business.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: While mobile data is good, heavy websites may load slowly. Optimize assets for mobile performance.

faqs.question: Is Google Ads effective?
faqs.answer: Less effective than social ads due to lower search volume, but good for targeting tourists/expats.

faqs.question: Do I need a license to advertise?
faqs.answer: Generally no, but specific products (alcohol, tobacco) have strict advertising bans.

faqs.question: What is the literacy rate?
faqs.answer: Adult literacy is ~70%, but youth literacy is very high. Visual content works best.
